description: PayPal operates in Israel including in settlements in the occupied West Bank, but does not grant Palestinians with West Bank and Gaza bank accounts access to its platform. Over five million Palestinians are excluded. Settlers, banks and merchants in the settlements use it freely on Israeli accounts.
energy_note: Same hillside. One side can get paid.

aspect: The stated reason, and the problem with it
description: PayPal cites a 'high risk' environment. It also operates in Somalia and Yemen. Palestinian-American businessman Sam Bahour notes Palestine has a functioning banking sector, all Palestinian banks have correspondent US banks making daily transfers, and the US Treasury has praised Palestinian banking compliance. Visa, Mastercard and Apple Pay operate there.
energy_note: Too risky for here, fine for Somalia.

aspect: Congress and shareholders have raised it and nothing changed
description: Eleven members of Congress wrote to the CEO before the May 2023 shareholder meeting. Harrington Investments, which pushed divestment from apartheid South Africa, filed a shareholder motion for a non-discrimination policy. The campaign has run since 2016.
Advocates argue the policy appears based on national or ethnic origin rather than location, which would breach the prohibition on discrimination in international human rights law.
energy_note: A geography rule that tracks an ethnicity exactly.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the comparison that undoes the risk argument
description: PayPal cites a 'high risk' environment for not serving Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. It operates in Somalia and Yemen. Visa, Mastercard and Apple Pay operate in the Palestinian territories, and the US Treasury has publicly praised Palestinian banking compliance.
energy_note: Too risky for Ramallah, acceptable in Mogadishu.
